Solution 13 (Similar Triangles and Lines)[edit]

The line between the hypotenuse and the corner of square S must be perpendicular to the hypotenuse, therefore creating a 90 degree angle with the hypotenuse.


There is a line parallel to the hypotenuse that contains the corner of square S, and that line is what is needed to find the side length of S.


We can extend the parallel line to the y-axis and figure out the equation for the line from here. With similar triangles, the length 2 is similar to the length 4, and the distance between the y-intercepts of the hypotenuse and this parallel line is 2.5 (similar to 5).


Since the hypotenuse has the equation y = -3x/4 + 3, we get the parallel line equation to be y = -3x/4 + 0.5. We know that the corner of S lies on the line y = x, so either coordinate value of the solution to the intersection of y = x and y = -3x/4 + 0.5 is the side length of the square. Solving this system, we get (2/7, 2/7), so S has a side length of 2/7. S has an area of 4/49, and subtracting this from the area of the triangle (6) you get 290/294 which can then be simplified to 145/147, or D.

~Solution by RafAhm123
